neighbours.label: the measured-quantity noun of a statistic, the thing being counted or rated (occupancy rates, units sold, million users, crime rates)
fire: Hotel occupancy rates in the city reached 91 percent during the festival.
The factory aims to raise annual production to 40,000 units by 2025.
By March the app had some 200 million registered users worldwide.
Burglary rates fell by 12 percent in the city last year.
Average room occupancy across the region was 78 percent in August.
The carmaker sold 1.2 million vehicles in the first half of the year.
Unemployment rates among young people rose to 15 percent this spring.
The airline carried 30 million passengers in its busiest year so far.
quiet: Hotels in the city were decorated with lights during the festival.
The factory hopes to hire new engineers and open a second line.
By March the app had added a dark mode and a new logo.
Burglars broke into a shop near the station last year.
Rooms across the region were booked by families in August.
The carmaker showed a new electric model at the spring fair.
Young people in the town said they wanted more jobs this spring.
The airline opened a new lounge in its busiest airport.

notes: Weak pole (max 8.6): occupancy, ocupación, million (users), units, crime (rates). The + pole is order value / spend over $. Near misses keep the topic without a statistic.
